scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8878: Users in both pods report the "web2.local" portal
returns nothing -- connections fail immediately instead of loading. The other
portals (web0/web1/web3) load fine. DNS resolves web2.local to 10.200.0.5,
and ping to 10.200.0.5 works from user machines. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_2

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: web_server_2 Apache (apache2) HTTP service
Mechanism: the apache2 service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) is stopped, so
  nothing listens on TCP/80 and connection attempts are refused immediately.
  Everything below the service layer is healthy: DNS still resolves
  web2.local -> 10.200.0.5, the OSPF path delivers packets (ping succeeds),
  and the other three web servers keep serving. The symptom is purely the
  dead HTTP daemon on one server.
Localization: web_server_2
Root cause: apache2 not running on web_server_2 (TCP/80 closed)
Fix: `service apache2 start` on web_server_2
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_2 (e.g. `service apache2 start`
/ `systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache listens on port 80 again,
http://web2.local serves normally. Nothing else needs changing.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-dns-and-network: notes DNS resolves web2.local correctly and 10.200.0.5 is reachable at the IP layer, ruling out name resolution and the network path

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the HTTP application service on web_server_2 (10.200.0.5), which hosts the “web2.local” portal. Network reachability and routing are healthy: users can ping 10.200.0.5 and other portals (web0/web1/web3) load normally, ruling out transport or OSPF issues.

Mechanism: Client HTTP connections to 10.200.0.5:80 fail immediately with near-zero connect and total times, which is characteristic of a TCP RST/connection refused rather than a timeout. Our timing tests from both a user host and the DNS server show connect: 0.000 and total ~0.0006–0.0015s to http://10.200.0.5, while a healthy server (http://10.200.0.3) shows non-zero connect/starttransfer times.

Localization: On the implicated device (web_server_2), there is no process listening on TCP/80. Netstat shows only the local resolver (127.0.0.11) and no 0.0.0.0:80 listener. Systemd reports apache2 is installed but inactive (dead), and nginx returns no status (not present or unmanaged). Thus, the interface web_server_2:eth0 is up, but the HTTP daemon is not bound to port 80.

Root cause: The web service on web_server_2 is stopped/not running, leaving port 80 closed.

Corrective fix: Start and enable the web server on web_server_2 (e.g., systemctl start apache2; systemctl enable apache2), or deploy/configure nginx, then verify it listens on 0.0.0.0:80 and serves the portal content. After starting, re-test with curl from a user host to confirm normal HTTP response times and content. Check logs if startup fails.

The log shows no process listening on :80 (netstat) and apache2 is inactive (systemctl), plus rapid zeroed connect times from curl consistent with immediate connection refusal; the agent's conclusion that apache2 is stopped on web_server_2 follows logically and covers key alternatives.
